Incorporating the Financial Stability Report, the statement’s macro tone remains moderately positive—strong labor market, low unemployment, and inflation near the 2 percent objective—supporting gradual normalization and an accommodative stance for now. However, the FSR tempers this positivity by noting elevated asset-valuation pressures and rising nonfinancial business leverage, even as bank capital and liquidity are strong and funding risks remain low. That mix—resilient core financial system but some late-cycle vulnerabilities—aligns with the Committee’s “balanced” risk assessment and data dependence, and it argues against an exuberant reading of the outlook despite solid business investment.

Netting these elements, the tone is moderately positive but more guarded than a purely macro read would suggest, so I nudge the sentiment slightly lower than the initial assessment.
